article.headline: Costco Holds Near 52-Week High As It Releases Holiday Product
article.deck: Costco sits 1.2% past its 1096.60 cup buy point, inside the buy range to 1151.43, but 3.22 ATRs above its 21-day line.
body: Costco slipped 3.66 to 1110.08 Tuesday, a 0.3% loss, two sessions after it broke out of a 25-week cup. The base ran 19.5% deep from its May 19 high to its Sept. 25 low and sets a buy point of 1096.60, with the buy range up to 1151.43. The close sits 1.2% above the buy point, inside the range. Volume ran 1.26x its 50-day average; the Nov. 13 breakout session traded 0.81x.

The stock closed 1.2% under its 52-week high of 1123.67. It sits 5.9% above its 21-day line at 1048.34 and 13.8% above its 50-day at 975.07, and at 3.22 ATRs from the 21-day line the tape is stretched even with the price still in range. RS rank is 92 of 99 on the desk's list, and the RS line is 3.7% below its high. Costco is up 28.7% this year and 20.3% over 12 months, and it is holding that ground in a market the desk reads as in correction.

In the quarter ended Aug. 31, EPS rose 15.0% to 6.75 and revenue rose 11.1% to $95.72 billion. The three quarters before printed EPS of 4.50, 4.58 and 4.93 on revenue of $67.31 billion, $69.60 billion and $70.53 billion. The next report is due Dec. 10. The stock trades at 44.3 times forward earnings on a $491.9 billion market cap.

TheStreet reported that Costco released a trendy holiday product, and an Investing.com piece said the stock sits near its 52-week high as panic buying looks priced in. After hours it traded at 1104.06, down 0.5% as of 6:10 p.m. Eastern, still above the buy point.
A close back under 1096.60 would make this a stalled breakout; a pause that lets the 21-day line catch up would ease the stretch.
article.watch: Watch the 1096.60 buy point on any dip ahead of the Dec. 10 report.

body: Tesla rose 0.37 to 380.11 Tuesday, up 0.1%, on volume 0.6x its 50-day average. The stock broke out of a seven-week flat base on Oct. 21, a session that traded 1.34x average, and has since slipped back below the 384.14 buy point. Tuesday's close sits 1.0% under it, so the breakout has stalled. The base ran 9.9% deep, and the buy range tops out at 403.35.

The pullback found the 50-day line: the stock bounced off it and closed 1.2% above it at 375.49. It sits 0.6% under its 21-day line at 382.31 and 0.6% under its 200-day at 382.27, and the 0.0 reading in ATRs from the 21-day line says the price is tangled with the short-term trend, not stretched. The flat base formed after a larger correction, and the stock is still 23.8% below the Dec. 22, 2025 high of 498.83. RS rank is 58 of 99 on the desk's list, and the RS line is 28.1% under its high. Tesla is down 15.5% this year and 6.0% over 12 months.

The numbers have not helped. September-quarter EPS fell 43.6% to 0.22 and revenue slipped 0.2% to $28.05 billion. The three quarters before printed EPS of 0.24, 0.13 and 0.32. The next report is due Jan. 27. The stock trades at 176.0 times forward earnings.

A close back above 384.14 puts it in the buy range again; a close under the 50-day line would undo the bounce.

body: Microsoft fell 14.44, or 2.8%, to 503.55 as of 11:48 a.m. Mountain. Nine sessions later it sits 9.1% below that buy point and well under the 581.51 top of the buy range. Today it is on pace for 0.88x its 50-day average volume.

That makes it a stalled breakout. The stock broke its 50-day line today, now 3.1% below the 519.55 average, and sits 4.1% under the 21-day line at 525.03, -0.61 ATRs from the 21-day line. The business is not the problem on the numbers given. The September quarter earned 4.92 a share, up 32.3% from a year earlier, on revenue of $92.28 billion, up 18.8%. Earnings ran 5.16, 4.27 and 4.81 in the three quarters before. The market cap is $3.74 trillion at 20.8 times forward earnings. The next report is due Jan. 27.

Investor's Business Daily reported software stocks retreated on inflation worries and a new OpenAI model, and Yahoo Finance covered service outages at JPMorgan, Microsoft, United and the FAA.

article.deck: Fastenal trades 2.5% above its 53.02 flat-base buy point, inside the buy range to 55.67, nine sessions after its breakout.
body: Fastenal sells the small parts that hold industry together: threaded fasteners, bolts, nuts, screws, studs and washers, plus a broad line of industrial and construction supplies. It distributes them wholesale in the United States, Canada, Mexico and abroad, to the plants, builders and maintenance crews that use them up every day.

The quarters show a business climbing step by step. EPS went from 0.26 in the December 2025 quarter to 0.30, 0.33 and 0.35 in the September quarter, which was up 20.7% from a year earlier. Revenue rose in each quarter in the table, from $2.03 billion to $2.20 billion, $2.39 billion and $2.46 billion, and the September quarter was up 15.5% year over year.

The market pays up for that steadiness. Fastenal carries a $62.4 billion market cap and trades at 44.2 times trailing and 38.4 times forward earnings. The stock is up 35.4% this year and 34.4% over 12 months.

On the chart, Fastenal broke out of a 12-week flat base on Nov. 4, a session that traded 1.48x its 50-day average volume. The base ran 10.6% deep from its Aug. 11 high to its Oct. 14 low and sets a buy point of 53.02, with the buy range up to 55.67. Tuesday the stock fell 0.76, or 1.4%, to 54.35 on volume 0.69x average. That leaves it 2.5% above the buy point and 3.4% below its 52-week high of 56.27.

The trend is orderly. The stock sits 1.7% above its 21-day line at 53.45 and 5.6% above its 50-day at 51.47, just 0.55 ATRs from the 21-day line, nowhere near stretched. RS rank is 82 of 99 on the desk's list, and the RS line is 0.4% below its high. After hours it traded at 54.03, down 0.6% as of 5:25 p.m. Eastern.

Zacks noted the stock is up 10.3% since its last earnings report, and 24/7 Wall St. pointed to its 35% gain in 2026. Fastenal shares the desk's industrial leadership with W.W. Grainger, also in its buy range, and both are holding up in a market the desk reads as in correction.
The next report is due Jan. 19. Until then the chart carries the story: a shallow base, a breakout that has held for nine sessions, and a price still inside its range.
article.watch: Watch the 21-day line at 53.45 and the 53.02 buy point just below it; a close under 53.02 would stall the breakout.

chief.verdict: The tape is in correction and the leaders show it: the Nasdaq sits 7.4% under its 50-day and 12.2% off its high, and the strength has rotated into defensive, slow-moving names like GWW, COST, AAPL, FAST and the drug stocks while AI chips have only 12% of their names above the 50-day. The setups that are working are tight flat bases in dull businesses, not growth breakouts. Risk leans down, so any buying should be small and only in the tightest charts.
chief.market: With the S&P 500 at 7 distribution days (weighted 7.2) and the Nasdaq at 6 (weighted 7.8), exposure should stay light, one or two small starter positions at most, until the Nasdaq gets back over its 50-day line.

picks.why: This is the best chart on the desk: a 15-week flat base only 12.9% deep, a breakout on 2.39 times normal volume, RS rank 93 with the RS line 0.9% from its high, and EPS up 102.9%. It is 3.3% past the 1420.01 buy point, still inside the range. The risk is that it closed down 1.9% today and sits 9.7% above the 50-day, so a weak market can pull it back to the pivot.
picks.entry: Buy range 1420.01 to 1491.01; the better entry is a pullback that holds the 21-day EMA near 1423.88 and the 1420.01 pivot, and a close back under 1420.01 means sell.

That is a breakout nobody bought in size. The risk is a quick fade back to the 1096.6 buy point.
